name: Trichocereus (Andean torch cacti)
status: 18 species; only those the ethnobotanical literature records as ceremonially active, tagged documented / reported / trace
notes: Loaded like the other catalogues (data/plants/*.json). Kew POWO files these under Echinopsis; the game uses the Trichocereus name with the synonym recorded. They grow only in cold, dry, high, rocky ground - Andean-type mountain bands - so on the planet they appear on the dry side of high ranges in the mild-temperature band. Bat/moth pollinated, one-night flowers; birds spread the fruit; fallen segments root, so clumps spread along slopes. Goats and other browsers do not eat them (cannot_be_browsed). Scope: the designer asked only for species with recorded ceremonial (psychoactive) use; the ceremony system reads the 'ceremonial' tag - 'documented' species carry a full ceremony, 'reported' a weaker one, 'trace' none (the oracle refuses them).

shrub.name: Trichocereus pachanoi

repro.note: Flowers open at night for a single night; fallen segments root where they land (clonal 'sucker' here means basal pups and rooted segments).

shrub.source: Andean columnar cactus; native region and habit from the standard cactus literature (Anderson, The Cactus Family, 2001; Kew POWO synonymy). Fast-growing, few-ribbed columns with short spines; branches from the base into a clump. Huge white night-opening flowers; red fruit. Synonym Echinopsis pachanoi.
